ui.title: Jiedong Zhang · Robotics & Embodied AI
ui.description: Jiedong Zhang: shape-aware motion planning, robot learning and computational physics.
ui.heroTag: Motion Planning · Robot Learning · Computational Physics
ui.heroLead: From the shape of a robot to the path it can follow.
ui.heroAbout: I work on shape-aware motion planning and robot learning, with a background in applied physics and a cross-university minor in mathematics. I enjoy building algorithms, connecting hardware and testing ideas on real robots.
ui.heroCurrent: Research intern at SJTU IITI · EvoMind and HKUST (Guangzhou) PAIRS Lab, working on robot learning and motion planning.
ui.piano: Classical piano — a continuing interest alongside research and engineering.
ui.fieldnotesIntro: Building, sharing and learning with other makers.

research.title: Shape-Aware Motion Planning
research.body: Collision-aware planning that accounts for the robot’s full shape, with an interest in articulated systems and coupled base–payload motion.

research.title: Robot Learning
research.body: Reinforcement-learning experiments, teacher–student distillation and history-based estimation for locomotion and whole-body control.

research.title: Vision–Language–Action
research.body: Model adaptation, dataset collection and cleaning, fine-tuning, and evaluation on robot hardware.

research.title: Computational Physics
research.body: Physics simulation and reproducible workflows that connect published methods, executable experiments and analysis figures.

projects.name: Shape-Aware Motion Planning
projects.body: Reproducing SVSDF collision-free motion planning from FAST Lab open-source code. Implemented SE(2) planning on a quadruped; SE(3) UAV trajectory planning is in progress. Exploring collision-aware planning for coupled base–payload and articulated systems.

projects.name: ATEC 2026 · Team ATEpi
projects.body: Led reinforcement-learning experiments and algorithm pipeline design. Reproduced HIMLoco, Extreme Parkour and whole-body control, using teacher–student distillation and history-based estimation. Scored 36/36 in obstacle traversal; placed 16th overall on the online L1 leaderboard, with a Track 2 score of 52.

projects.name: Anisotropic Complex-Plasma Simulation
projects.body: Developed a Taichi/PyTorch simulation engine for anisotropic complex plasma and reproduced published research. Built experiment-data archiving tools with memU and the Claude-Scientist backend. Completed a national-level undergraduate innovation project and graduation thesis, supporting ISS data-processing work.
projects.caption: A simulation result from my public project repository: two-temperature dynamics in a reproduction of Ivlev et al., PRX (2015).

projects.name: Agentcraft · AR / AI Glasses
projects.body: Designed and implemented a 2D-to-3D interaction pipeline using Tripo3D, 3DGS and AI glasses. Integrated WorldGen and World Labs tools and APIs to validate two prototypes. The team received the Technical Innovation Award at Rokid Spatial Joy 2025.
projects.caption: Agentcraft’s trophy and certificate for the Rokid Spatial Joy 2025 Technical Innovation Award, received in January 2026.

experience.body: Collected, cleaned and organized active visual tracking data. Trained and tested PI0 / PI0.5 on Piper; used Qwen-4B for fine-tuning and data generation.

Adapted starVLA to benchmark tasks, calibrated an extended seven-axis SO101 arm, deployed Jetson Orin, and connected Quest 3 teleoperation to OPENARM. Fifth author of Evo-RL, submitted to ICRA 2027; contributed figures, manuscript preparation and detailed review.
Supported AR technical sharing, campus liaison and XR collaboration. Discussed developer and user needs at S-Startup, Google DevFest and AdventureX.
Helped organize hackathons through the NJU Maker Club, coordinated sponsorship resources, and supported collaboration in a maker community of more than 500 members.
